This is a claim petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.

2. The case of the petitioner is that on 24-06-2020 at about 09-00 a.m. while she was proceeding on a Cont'd..., MVC No. 2404 /2020 motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-51-R-6223 as a pillion rider near Agasanakere, Malavalli Taluk at that time the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-10-A- 5099 was said to be plying from opposite direction driven in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed the Motor Cycle causing RTA, whereby the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately she was said to be shifted to the Malavalli Government Hospital.
Later she shifted to M. S. Ramaiah Hospital for further treatment.
Criminal case is said to have registered against the said vehicle in Crime No. 107/2020 by the concerned police.
Respondent No.1 is said to be the owner and respondent No. 2 is the insurer.
The respondents are said to be liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, filed the petition.
After receipt of notice, the respondent No. 1 did not appear before this Court.
Hence, the respondent No. 1 has been placed exparte.

4. Respondent No.2 has filed objection and the contention is that RTA said to have taken place due to the carelessness and negligence of the rider of motorcycle, who was said to be proceeding on the road without following the Traffic Rules.
Respondent No.2 in the objection has contended that the Insurance Policy said to have been issued in the name of respondent No.1 and that the policy was in force as on the date of the RTA.
The liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.
The respondent No.2 has filed objection.

The Respondent No.2 in the objection has admitted that Cont'd..., MVC No. 2404 /2020 respondent No.1 to be the owner and respondent No.2 to be its insurer and that the policy was inforce as on the date of the RTA.
The RTA according to the respondent No.2 is said to have taken place due to the negligent act of the rider of motorcycle and therefore the owner and insurer of the said vehicle are not liable.
The liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy, valid and effective driving license of the vehicle.
Denying all the other averments of the petition the respondent No. 2 had sought for the dismissal of the claim petition.

5. The court had framed the following :-
ISSUES Sudharani.

On the other hand, respondent No. 2 not led evidence and no documents got marked on behalf of respondent No. 2.

The findings on the above issues are as follows Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :

Cont'd..., MVC No. 2404 /2020  front rear right wheel damaged.

 crash guard right side damaged  head light and mask damaged  front right side indicator damaged The charge sheet Ex. P-3 has been filed for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC and also under Section 187 of IMV Act.
The above discussed documentary evidence and the oral evidence of PW1 are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicle Act.
The above discussed documents goes to show that there is no iota of evidence about the negligence attributed against the rider of motorcycle.
Therefore, it is mere contention without any kind of supporting Cont'd..., MVC No. 2404 /2020 documents.

At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."

The oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act and hence the issue No. 1 is answered in the "affirmative" .

Hospital has issued a discharge summary as per Ex. P-8 and it shows that she was admitted on 24-06-2020 and discharged on 29-06-2020.
In the column pertaining to Cont'd..., MVC No. 2404 /2020 clinical features, there is mention about tenderness and swelling to be present.
There is also mention about the investigation to have been conducted and that there was right distal femur communited fracture open type 3B.
Ex. P-9 are medical bills and they amount to Rs.30,460/-.
It is also the contention of the respondent that the petitioner admitted that even after accident, has continued her profession.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation towards loss of future income.
11. The learned counsel for the petitioner has adduced the evidence of the Medical Officer as PW-2.
Medical Officer is said to have examined this petitioner and he has given 43% permanent disability in respect of left lower limb and 14% to the whole body.
The condition of Cont'd...
, MVC No. 2404 /2020 the petitioner is said to be Non-Progressive.
X-rays have been marked as Ex. P-14.
The age of this petitioner is as per the wound certificate 32 years.
The discharge summary mentions age as 32 years.

With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar -vs- Ajay Kumar and Another wherein it has been held as follows ;-
A. Motor Vehicles Act 1988, - Ss.166, 163-A and Sch.II - Permanent disability - Compensation - Award of - Assessment of loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability - Detailed principles for, laid down - Functional disability as operative criterion distinguished from physical disability - Disability certificate - Mode of assessment based upon - Types of disability, distinguished - held, in disability certificate extent of disability of a limb (or part of the body) cannot be assumed to be extent of disability of whole body - Tribunal should not mechanically apply percentage of permanent Cont'd..., MVC No. 2404 /2020 physical disability as percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity, but must assess functional disability - Directions given to Tribunals in respect of procedure/steps to be followed in such cases - Tort Law - Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, Ss.3,
4 and Schs.I and IV.
B. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Ss.166, 163-A and Sch.II - Permanent disability - Compensation - Injured claimant, cheese vendor, sustaining fracture of both bones of left leg and fracture of left radius - Tribunal assuming 45% disability as shown in disability certificate as economic disability -
In appeal, high Court rejected increase in compensation on ground that disability certificate as not reliable - sustainability - held, High Court ought not to have rejected disability certificate -

Tribunal overlooked fact that disability certificate referred to 45% disability to left lower limb and not to functional disability of the body - Permanent functional disability of body assessed as 25%, loss of future earning capacity as 25% - In cases of injured claimant with a disability, no need to deduct one- third out of income towards personal and living expenses.
C. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Ss.166, 163-A and Sch.II - Permanent disability - Validity of disability certificate.

12. The nature of the work of this petitioner for his earning is said to be nurse.
Therefore, his earning was said to be Rs.33,000/- and that she is the only earning member of the family.
In the absence of any documents with regard to the earning, educational qualifications of the petitioner RTA is dated 24-06-2020.
Hence, it is appropriate to assess the income of this petitioner as Rs.14,500/-.
The liability is to be applied in terms of the decision reported in AIR 2009 SC 3226 and the appropriate multiplier would be '16'.
Therefore, the yearly income would be Rs.1,74,000/-.

Considering this nature of avocation, the Cont'd..., MVC No. 2404 /2020 disability from the materials placed before the court is assessed at 10% and therefore 1,74,000 x 10/100= 17,400 x16(multiplier)=
Rs.2,78,400/- and that will be the future loss of income on account of disability.

13. Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, age of the petitioner, nature of the documents produced before the court therefore it is appropriate to award sum of Rs. 50,000/-
towards pain and sufferings.
He must have been put in lot of inconvenience which entitles him for a sum of Rs. 50,000/- for loss of amenities.
The medical bills amount to Rs.30,460/-.
Immediately after the RTA he must have been not able to do any kind of work for a period of three months which entitles him for a sum of Rs.43,500/-.
He Cont'd...
, MVC No. 2404 /2020 must have been on diet and incurred transportation expenditure which entitles him for a sum of Rs. 6,000/-.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for the following heads of compensation.

Heads of compensation amount in Rs.
1. Pain and sufferings 50,000/-
2. Loss of amenities 50,000/-
3. Future loss of income on account 2,78,400/-
of disability 4. Loss of income during laid up 43,500/-
period 5.

ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.4,58,360/ (Rupees Four lakh fifty eight thousand three hundred and sixty only) and are entitled for interest at 6% per annum from the date of the petition till its realization.
Respondents are jointly and  severally liable to pay the  compensation amount.
